events.text: You are a baby, and you remember a whole life. The words are right there on your tongue. A parent is leaning over the cradle.

effects.log: "Good morning." The rice bowl hits the floor. By evening the whole village has come to see the talking baby.

choices.text: Babble like a baby. Hide what you are

effects.log: Goo. Ga. Your family laughs. Nobody suspects a thing, and in the murim that is worth more than fame.

events.text: Lying in the dark, you remember how breathing methods begin: the lower dantian, the slow count. Your tiny body could start now.

choices.text: Circulate qi every night in secret

ok.log: A thread of warmth answers you, years early. Three-year-olds are not supposed to have internal energy. You do.

fail.log: The qi goes the wrong way and you cry all night. Your family thinks it is teething.

choices.text: Wait. A child's meridians are fragile

effects.log: Patience is also something you learned in your last life.

events.text: A parent leaves a ledger open on the table. You can read every character. At three.

choices.text: Point out the mistake in the sums

effects.log: They check it three times. You were right. They look at you for a long moment and say nothing, then buy you a brush.

choices.text: Pretend it is a picture book

effects.log: You turn it upside down and giggle. Some secrets are safer kept until you can hold a sword.

events.text: A cold feeling. You remember this day from your past life: the river floods tonight, and the lower houses are swept away.

choices.text: Throw a tantrum until the family moves uphill

effects.log: Everyone thinks you are being impossible, until the river comes at midnight. Afterwards the old women call you a little oracle.

choices.text: Say nothing. You cannot explain how you know

effects.log: The flood comes. You lie awake listening to it and learn how heavy knowing can be.

events.text: A wandering master stops at your gate for water and watches you play with a stick. Your footwork is a sword form from your past life.

effects.log: His cup stops halfway to his mouth. "Who taught you that?" You shrug. He leaves a jade token: "When you are older, come find me."

choices.text: Trip over the stick on purpose

effects.log: He laughs and moves on. Better that the murim does not notice you yet.

events.text: Your mind is old but your body is tiny. You try a stance you used to hold for an hour and fall over after a breath.

choices.text: Train the body anyway, a little every day

effects.log: Bruises, then fewer bruises. By five you can hold the stance for a count of a hundred.

choices.text: Laugh at yourself and enjoy being small

effects.log: You nap in the sun like a cat. There will be time enough for training. This time you know it.
